en: Of this mantra of the hymn for increasing glorious wisdom (Śrīprajñāvivardhana), Sanatkumāra is the seer (ṛṣi);
Lord Kārttikeya is the deity; Anuṣṭubh is the meter;
and its application (viniyoga) is in recitation for the sake of attaining all branches of knowledge.
The lord of yogis, Mahāsena, Kārtikeya, the son of Agni, Skanda, Kumāra, the commander-in-chief, born from Lord Śaṅkara. ||1||
Gāṅgeya, Tāmracūḍa, Brahmacārī, Śikhidhvaja, Tārakāri—the son of Umā—and Krauñcāri—Ṣaḍānana. ||2||
And the ocean of the Word-Brahman (Śabdabrahma), the perfected one Sārasvata Guha, the Lord Sanatkumāra, who bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation. ||3||
Born in the reed-thicket, the elder brother of Gaṇeśa, the maker of the path to liberation, the propounder of all scriptures, and the revealer of desired objects. ||4||
He who, endowed with faith, recites these twenty-eight names of mine at dawn shall become the Lord of Speech, even if he were previously mute. (5)
The recitation of my names consists of great mantras;
one attains great wisdom—there is no need for deliberation on this matter. (6)
